failure_patterns.pattern: rule_wrong: Geographic answers were expanded with a generic term even though the expected conventional label omits it.

rejected_edits.content:
## Use the Conventional Geographic Label
Use the complete geographic label conventional in the clue and context; do not mechanically expand or shorten it. Retain a generic term such as “Lake,” “Mount,” or “River” when it is part of the requested conventional label, but do not append one merely because it describes the entity's type. A context that identifies a place as a river or mountain range does not by itself establish that the answer label must include that word.
rejected_edits.target:
## Preserve Full Canonical Geographic Names
When a geographic proper name conventionally includes a generic component such as “Lake,” “Mount,” or “River,” retain that component in the answer. Do not shorten the name to its modifier unless the context or clue establishes the shortened form as the requested label.

rejected_edits.content: For proper names and titles, use the conventional form that identifies the requested entity. Do not substitute a nickname or later brand name for the historically relevant label, omit words from a work's title when the work is requested, or add optional middle names. Prefer the shortest complete conventional name that fills the slot: a search-result heading or formal company name does not require copying an extra corporate suffix or descriptive word when the clue asks for the commonly used name. Retain components integral to a title or established name; when the clue requests a generic class, do not embellish it with a narrower associated name.
